a1_t.text: ART PASS v1 — World & art direction. Awaiting approval of the core cast + live match before anything propagates to pages 00–19.

a2_t.text: Three character routes on the same rig and pose set, judged on the same tests. Route A is recommended.

a3_t.text: Core cast: 8 dealmakers. The full character comes first, then portrait → bust → avatar → icon.

a4_t.text: Pose & expression system: 14 states × 8 characters, all from one rig. Expressions are driven only by public game events.

a5_t.text: Hero asset art + three environment families, each built in seven depth layers around a calm centre where the opponent stands.

a6_mnote.text: Mobile keeps the same four facts in the same places, top to bottom: THEIR plaque (their side) → gap rail → MY sealed card + the one seal button in the thumb zone → MY limit card and the turn-clock by my hands. Chat opens as a sheet from the chat knob.

a6_stop.text: STOP HERE. The new art direction has NOT been applied to pages 00–19. Approve the core cast + this live match first, then I propagate it to onboarding, result, the Bay and the rest.

a6_t.text: Revised live match: first person, across the table. Desktop + mobile, the comparison with the current screen, the blur test and the acceptance checklist.

a7_t.text: Updated art / character design system (K): style spec, audit of the current product, rejected shortcuts and production rules.

an_t.text: Post-match analysis & replay — a scoreboard, not a report

b2_n.text:
ONE NEAR-TERM REASON, ONE AT A TIME (priority order)
1 Placement n/5 (new players)
2 Rival asked for a rematch (shown as the rival standing on the dock)
3 Today’s Deal not played (the bottle glows)
4 Points to next division
5 New personal best / style profile completing
The objective chip shows the highest one; others live in the world (rival, bottle) — never as a card grid.

b2_n2.text: PROGRESSIVE UNLOCK — see 00 · Unlock map. New players see RANKED · TODAY’S DEAL · PRACTICE only. “Right now” rows appear only when real: an event you can join, an invitation, a promoted rotating mode. Friend Challenge unlocks after your first human deal.

b2_t.text: The Bay v2 — a place, not a dashboard. One objective, one big button, the rest lives in the world

bl_t.text: The strict test — all text blurred

j2_pdr.text: PRODUCT DECISION REQUIRED · “Verified information reveal” is not defined in the approved rules. Choreography assumes a verified fact about the asset becomes visible to BOTH players mid-match. If it is private intel, only the slip + stamp play, and only on the receiver’s side.

j2_t.text: Every event × 10 dimensions: anticipation, motion, impact, secondary, character, world, sound, haptic, duration, reduced motion.

l2_n1.text:
WHAT CHANGED (v2)
• The stall, GOLDENOTTER and the compass are the structure; UI floats on them.
• The price rail became the counter’s brass rail: the physical distance between the two plaques IS the gap. Close = gold glow. Crossed = green, counter lights up.
• Always on: their plaque, your plaque, your wax-sealed limit, the turn banner.
• Context only: chips (while composing), bounty token (while your clock runs), chat (a speech bubble + the chat button), history (ledger button), walk away (⋯ menu).

l2_n2.text:
ONE DOMINANT DECISION per state
Your turn, far apart → compose (MAKE OFFER).
Your turn, close or crossed → ACCEPT becomes the big green button; MAKE OFFER drops to secondary.
Their turn → nothing to press; watch them think.

l2_pdr.text: PRODUCT DECISION REQUIRED — D1 chip cost curve · D7 accept on their turn · D10 offers above own limit · opponent resources hidden (drawn).

l2_t1.text: Live match v2 — you are facing GOLDENOTTER across a market counter. Four things always on: THEIR OFFER · YOUR OFFER · YOUR LIMIT · WHOSE TURN

m2_n.text: The top half is never covered by UI except the turn banner and name sign. Composer, chat bar and ACCEPT live in the thumb zone. The chat sheet stops at the counter edge so both plaques, the rail and the wax seal stay readable while you type.

m2_t1.text: Live match v2 — mobile: opponent + asset own the top half; one thumb-zone decision at the bottom

ob_n1.text:
TUTORIAL RULES
• One concept per lesson; the player acts first, then we name what happened (T3 explains irreversibility only after the first offer).
• The Harbourmaster is labelled AI on every frame; tutorial deals are unrated.
• No ZOPA/BATNA jargon. An optional “Why?” link on T7 can explain the bargaining range.
• Skip tutorial is always available; skipping still requires one practice deal before ranked (D13).

ob_pdr.text: PRODUCT DECISION REQUIRED — D13 can a new player skip straight to ranked? D14 guest play: may a visitor from a friend link play before creating an account? Drawn: account first on the main funnel; friend-link guests allowed (see 12 · Friends).

pv1_t.text: The system under the story: one loop, one information boundary, one hero per state, and a hard line between offers and talk.

pv2_t.text: One live negotiation between two people, frame by frame, seen from the buyer's seat. Then two shorter stories: an honest wall, and a bluff that was read right and still lost.

pv3_t.text: The poker moment: hidden limits turn over one at a time. Then the volume rules for every human event.

pv4_t.text: Why they come back: the other side of the same deal, and the same person again.

r2_n.text:
THREE BEATS, then the next match
1 · DEAL 74 — plaque slams green on the counter (1.2 s, auto)
2 · YOU CAPTURED 63% — both wax seals break, split bar fills (tap)
3 · +18 and one deterministic insight — REMATCH is the biggest thing on screen
Everything else (bargaining range chart, chips, multiplier, bounty maths, replay) is one level deeper: “Breakdown”.

r2_pdr.text: PRODUCT DECISION REQUIRED — D2 bounty formula (not shown in the 3 beats; lives in Breakdown) · D3 rating deltas · D12 do roles swap on rematch · D20 insight rule priority (drawn: concession total comparison; alternatives: opening anchor, time used, largest single move).

sc_n.text: Role colour never changes: YOU are always ember, whatever your role. BUYER/SELLER is a label, not a colour. The brief text is flavour; the number on the vault card is the only binding figure. “TAKE YOUR SEAT” auto-starts at 0:00 so a slow reader can’t stall the opponent (D16: reveal countdown length).
